In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] field of [[graph theory]], the '''Robertson graph''' or '''(4,5)-cage''', is a 4-[[regular graph|regular]] [[undirected graph]] with 19 vertices and 38 edges named after [[Neil Robertson (mathematician)|Neil Robertson]].<ref>{{MathWorld|urlname=RobertsonGraph|title=Robertson Graph}}</ref><ref>Bondy, J. A. and Murty, U. S. R. Graph Theory with Applications. New York: North Holland, p. 237, 1976.</ref>

The Robertson graph is the unique [[cage graph|(4,5)-cage graph]] and was discovered by Robertson in 1964.<ref>Robertson, N. "The Smallest Graph of Girth 5 and Valency 4." Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 70, 824-825, 1964.</ref> As a cage graph, it is the smallest 4-regular graph with girth 5.

It has [[chromatic number]] 3, [[chromatic index]] 5, diameter 3, radius 3 and is both  4-[[k-vertex-connected graph|vertex-connected]] and 4-[[k-edge-connected graph|edge-connected]]. It has [[book thickness]] 3 and [[queue number]] 2.<ref>Jessica Wolz, ''Engineering Linear Layouts with SAT''. Master Thesis, University of Tübingen, 2018</ref> 
The graph is neither planar nor [[1-planar_graph|1-planar]].<ref>{{citation
 | last = Pupyrev | first = Sergey
 | editor-first1 = Vida | editor-last1 = Dujmović | editor-first2 = Fabrizio | editor-last2 = Montecchiani
 | contribution = OOPS: Optimized One-Planarity Solver via SAT
 | title = Proc. 33rd International Symposium on Graph Drawing and Network Visualization (GD 2025)
 | series = Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics (LIPIcs)
 | year = 2025 | volume = 357 | pages = 14:1–14:19
 | doi = 10.4230/LIPIcs.GD.2025.14
 | isbn = 978-3-95977-403-1 | doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

The Robertson graph is also a [[Hamiltonian graph]] which possesses {{formatnum:5376}} distinct directed Hamiltonian cycles.

The Robertson graph is one of the smallest graphs with [[cop number]] 4.<ref name="ROB4">Turcotte, J., & Yvon, S. (2021). 4-cop-win graphs have at least 19 vertices. Discrete Applied Mathematics, 301, 74-98.</ref>

==Algebraic properties==
The Robertson graph is not a [[vertex-transitive graph]]; its full automorphism group is isomorphic to the [[dihedral group]] of order 24, the group of symmetries of a regular [[dodecagon]], including both rotations and reflections.<ref name="SURV">Geoffrey Exoo & Robert Jajcay, Dynamic cage survey, Electr. J. Combin. 15, 2008.</ref>

The [[characteristic polynomial]] of the Robertson graph is
:<math>(x-4)(x-1)^2(x^2-3)^2(x^2+x-5)</math>
:<math>(x^2+x-4)^2(x^2+x-3)^2(x^2+x-1).\ </math>
